Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Shiv Kumar vs Damodar Prasad Sahu & Ors
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts necessary for disposal of the present appeal in brief are that on 31.03.2002 the appellant was travelling in the tractor trolley bearing registration no. MP-20H/6642 in the capacity of labourer, on the way, the vehicle got punctured.
The respondent no.1/driver instructed him to hold the jack while changing the stepney.

The respondent no.1 negligently removed the jack due to which the trolley fell on the hands of the appellant and both his hands were badly injured and he suffered permanent disability upto 10% in his hands.

4. The respondents have submitted in their written statement that neither any accident has accrued,
nor applicant has suffered any injury by the tractor trolley in issue, neither any boney fracture, nor any permanent disability has been caused to him.
Respondent no.3/Insurance Company has also denied the claim and submitted that the FIR was lodged delayed and the nature of injuries was also not mentioned.
5. After taking the evidence from both the sides, learned tribunal has rejected the application of the applicant.

6. It is submitted by the learned counsel of appellant/claimant that the learned tribunal has erred in appreciating that F.I.R. is duly corroborates the case of the appellant and the evidence brought forward by him in support of his contentions by independent - witnesses Vishnu (PW/3) and Nanhelal (PW/4) and the claimant has remained successful in proving his case.

The nature of injury and the fact that appellant has sustained permanent disability upto 10% has been found proved by the learned tribunal as the appellant/claimant has sustained grievous injury on the fingers of the both hands.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel of appellant/claimant that the applications under Sections 140 and 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, was disputed only by respondents no. 1 and 2 and not by respondent no.3 despite that the learned tribunal has erred in dismissing the claim petition.
7. Per Contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 that the learned tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation in favour of the claimant.
8. Having heard the learned counsel of the parties and on perusal of record.

It is found that the case of claimant is that at the time of accident, the tyre of tractor trolley bearing registration no.MP-20H/6642 was got punctured on the way and the respondent no.1 instructed him to hold the jack.
While changing the stepney and respondent no.1 very negligently removed the jack and as a result the trolley fell onto the hands of the appellant and both his hands were badly injured.

This case of the appellant/claimant is supported by the FIR (Ex.P/1) which is filed on behalf of the appellant and other documents in support thereto filed on behalf of the applicant.
9.
Appellant in his evidence also supported its case and he remained intact in cross-examination.

He stated categorically in his examination that in application under Section 140 of Motor Vehicle Act,
he has not got written the fact that the injuries sustained by him due to the accident caused by a truck.

In this regard, perusal of record shows that the application under Section 140 of the M.V. Act Shiv Kumar vs Damodar Prasad Sahu & Ors on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66047144/
2 was earlier have been filed on behalf of the appellant/claimant containing the fact that at the time of changing tyre, suddenly a truck came there and dashed, therefore, the appellant sustained injuries.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, thereafter, other application under Section 140 of M.V. Act filed on 10/7/2002 and it is stated therein that this application be read with earlier application containing the full facts regarding the accident.

This application was decided by the learned tribunal vide order dated 11/8/2003 in which the learned counsel of the claimant stated that earlier application mistakenly drafted by the clerk of advocate and, thereafter, the corrected application has been filed.

Therefore,
the learned tribunal has based his finding upon earlier application u/s 140 of the M.V. Act cannot be said to be legal and maintainable.
10. It is revealed from the record that in support of the application, Shiv Kumar has deposed before the learned tribunal and he remained intact in cross-examination on the accident.

Though the witness Karan Singh (AW/2) didn't support the case of the appellant but witnesses Vishnu (AW/3)
and Nanhelal (AW/4) supported the statement of appellant as well as the case of the appellant.
The testimony of these witnesses cannot be dis-believed on the basis that they were not named in the witness list of the challan filed by prosecution.

It is pertinent to be mentioned here that charge sheet containing the witness list is not on record and it cannot be said in absence of such document that these witnesses were not listed in witness list of the prosecution.
Both these witnesses remained intact in the cross-examination.

11. Non-applicant no.1 Damodar has examined himself in defence, who denied the factum of accident but he admits in cross-examination that Ramdayal/non-applicant no.2 is his father and the registered owner of the offending vehicle.

The tractor trolley was remained standing at the place of occurrence though he denied the factum of accident as stated by the appellant but he admits in cross-examination that a criminal case under Sections 279 and 338 is being proceeded against him and he didn't complaint before any authority against continuation of 'such false case' against him.

Therefore, the deposition of non-applicant no.1 Damodar is not found believable vis--vis the witnesses examined on behalf of the appellant, which is supported by the documentary evidence on the record.
Therefore, the finding of learned tribunal that the appellant/claimant has failed to prove the factum of accident is not maintainable.

12. So far as, the permanent disability to the appellant is concerned though the learned tribunal has found 10% permanent disability to the appellant/claimantbut it revealed from the record that though the appellant has filed permanent disability certificate as Ex.P/6 but he neither examined any doctor or any member of the medical board, who have said to issue the certificate.
Mere exhibition is not sufficient to prove this document.

It was incumbent on the applicant to examine any member of District Disability Board, who has issued this certificate by their signatures but appellant is failed to do so for the reasons best known to him.

In absence of such evidence, 10%
permanent disability caused to the appellant is not found proved.

But having regard to the x-ray report and x-ray plates filed by the appellant, it is found that the phalanx of fingers of right hand and left hand were fractured and therefore, appellant has sustained grievous injuries on the finger of both the hands Shiv Kumar vs Damodar Prasad Sahu & Ors on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66047144/
3 13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though, the learned tribunal has not assessed the compensation amountbut since the incident was of year 2002 and after 22 years, it would not be in the interest of justice to remand the case to learned tribunal to assess the amount of compensation.
In the considered view of this court and having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant, the compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- would suffice.

It is pleaded by the appellant that he was labour and receiving Rs.100/-
per day wages.

Therefore, assuming Rs. 3000/- per month salary of the appellant, three months'
salary is ought to have been granted in favour of the claimant/appellant.
Therefore, in total, the appellant/claimant is entitled to get Rs.39,000/- as compensation.

14. Consequently, the appellant is entitled to get the compensation amount of Rs.39,000/- from respondents jointly and severally with the interest @ 6% p.a. on the compensation amount from the date of application.
15. In the result, the Misc. Appeal filed on behalf of the appellant/claimant is partly allowed by setting aside the impugned awardin the terms stated above.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE m/-
